test_title: PYST 41: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 25 Feb, 2025 - Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Mukund has two grandsons Sachin and Chetan. 13 year old Sachin gets some money from Mukund’s wealth and 14 year old Chetan gets rest of the money. But Sachin and Chetan will get money only when they turn 23 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 10% compounded annually. When both turn 23, they receive the same amount. How much had Mukund given Chetan (in ₹) initially, if total money with Mukund was ₹25200?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Time difference for Sachin (23 − 13 = 10 yrs) and Chetan (23 − 14 = 9 yrs) is 1 year.

When compound amounts are equal, the principal ratio is inversely proportional to the accumulating factor (1 + R/100)T.

Ratio of Chetan's share to Sachin's share = (1 + 10/100)¹ : 1 = 11 : 10.

Chetan's share = 11 / (11 + 10) × 25200 = (11 / 21) × 25200 = 13200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total money = ₹25200

Sachin's age = 13 years, Chetan's age = 14 years

Time for Sachin (T₁) = 23 − 13 = 10 years

Time for Chetan (T₂) = 23 − 14 = 9 years

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest = P × (1 + R/100)T
